transcript.text: Water started coming into my basement last night after the storm. I don't know who to call.

One safety note first: if the water is near outlets, cords, appliances, or your electrical panel, stay out of the water. Only turn off power to the basement at the breaker if you can reach the panel without standing in water. If you can't, leave the power on and stay out of the basement.

Two quick questions so I can find someone near you:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. About how deep is the water, and is it still coming in?
It's 94087. Maybe 2 inches across the floor, coming in along the back wall, and the outlets aren't underwater, thankfully.

Good that the outlets are dry. Here are the best matches near Sunnyvale:

my furnace stopped working and the house is getting really cold

I'm sorry, that's miserable, especially when it's cold out. First, a quick safety check: if you smell gas (a rotten-egg smell) or a carbon monoxide alarm is going off, get everyone outside and call 911 or your gas utility from outside.

If not, I'll find a heating pro near you. Two quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code, or your city and state?
2. What's the furnace doing? For example: blowing cold air, not turning on at all, or clicking without lighting. And have you checked the thermostat and the furnace's power switch or breaker?
no gas smell. 94087, sunnyvale. fan runs but it's blowing cold air since this morning, already put new batteries in the thermostat

Thanks, that helps. When the fan runs but the air stays cold, the burner usually isn't lighting. Common causes are a dirty igniter or flame sensor, a safety switch that tripped because of a clogged filter, or a gas valve or control board problem. Before a tech comes, two safe things to check:
- The thermostat is set to Heat, and the fan is on Auto, not On. With the fan on On, it blows room-temperature air all the time.
- The furnace filter. If it's very dirty, swapping it and turning the furnace off and back on can sometimes get it going again.

One of the outlets in my kitchen sparked and now half the kitchen has no power.

That sounds scary. I'm glad you're okay. Here's what to do for safety right now:

- Don't plug anything into that outlet or touch it. Unplug anything that's in it only if the plug isn't scorched or hot.
- If you smell burning, see smoke, or the outlet or wall feels warm, get everyone out and call 911.
- Check your electrical panel. A tripped breaker or a GFCI outlet that has "popped" is likely why half the kitchen lost power. Don't reset it yet. Leave that circuit off until an electrician has looked at the outlet. If the breaker didn't trip and the outlet still looks live, turn that breaker off if you can safely reach the panel. Don't do this if there's water near the panel.

I'll find a licensed electrician near you. Two quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. Do you see any scorch marks or melting on the outlet, or smell burning?

ZIP is 94087. No burning smell now, but there's a faint dark mark around one of the slots. The breaker tripped yesterday evening and I tried resetting it a couple times but it trips right away, so I've left it off.

Good call leaving that breaker off. A breaker that trips again as soon as you reset it usually means there's a short on that circuit, and the dark mark points to that outlet as the likely spot. It isn't something to keep resetting. With the circuit off you're safe for now, but you'll want an electrician in the next day or so.

Before I send all that, why do you need to know whether I own or rent? And will Flores Electric get my email too, or just my phone number?

Both fair questions.

Why owner vs. renter: if you rent, the landlord or property manager usually has to approve electrical work and is often the one who pays. Your lease may also say repairs have to go through them. The electrician wants to know that up front so they don't show up and then can't start. If you rent, it's worth giving your landlord a heads-up too. Property type helps them plan access and any permit needs. You don't have to answer either one; I can mark them as unknown.

Your email: Flores Electric only gets what you give me. Email is optional. If you leave it out, they just get your name, phone number, the service address and the job details. If you do include it, it goes to them along with the rest. Before anything is sent, I'll confirm exactly what's being shared and ask for your okay.

Hi, there's a brown stain spreading on my ceiling, I think the roof is leaking

Sorry you're dealing with that. A spreading ceiling stain usually means water is getting in somewhere above it, and catching it early saves a lot of drywall and insulation damage.

A quick safety note: if the stain is near a light fixture or the ceiling is sagging or bulging, turn off that circuit at the breaker and keep people out from under it. A sagging spot can hold pooled water.

Two quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code (or city and state)?
2. Is water actively dripping right now, or is it just a stain so far? Does it get worse when it rains?

Thanks for the tip, it's not near a light and it isn't sagging, just a stain about the size of a dinner plate in the hallway. I'm in Sunnyvale, CA 94087, and it's not dripping right now, only during heavy rain.

Good, no sagging and no active drip. That makes this a "soon" job rather than an emergency, but you'll want it fixed before the next big storm. Water often travels along rafters before it drips, so the actual leak may not be right above the stain. A roofer will usually check the attic and the flashing around vents or chimneys.

kitchen sink totally clogged, water won't go down at all

That's annoying, especially with a sink full of water. A clogged kitchen sink is a job for a plumber, and I can find one near you.

A couple of quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code, or your city and state?
2. Is it just the kitchen sink that's backed up, or are other drains (like the dishwasher, bathroom sinks, tubs or toilets) slow or backing up too? Have you tried anything yet, like a plunger or drain cleaner?

Until it's fixed, try not to run the dishwasher or garbage disposal. Either one can push more water into the sink.
Sunnyvale CA, 94087. Just the kitchen sink, both sides have standing water since last night. I tried a plunger and some Drano, and the disposal just hums but won't spin.

Thanks, that helps. Two safety notes first:
- There's Drano in that standing water now, so don't plunge any more. It can splash lye onto your skin or into your eyes. The plumber needs to know it's in there.
- Turn the disposal off and leave it off. Running it while it hums can burn out the motor.

Since both sides are backed up and the disposal is jammed, the clog is probably in the shared drain line. A plumber can clear the line and check the disposal on the same visit.

how much does it cost to fix a water heater

I can't give you a price, even a rough one. It really depends on what the technician finds, and the provider will give you a quote. When I send your request, I can add a note saying you want the diagnostic/trip fee and a written quote before any work starts.

I can explain what's likely going on and find a local plumber. Two quick questions:

1. What's the water heater doing? For example, no hot water, not enough hot water, leaking, strange noises, or a pilot light that won't stay lit. Is it gas, electric or tankless, and do you know roughly how old it is?
2. What's your ZIP code?

One safety note: if it's a gas unit and you smell gas, leave the house now and call your gas utility or 911 from outside.
It's a gas tank, 40 gallons, about 12 years old. Only lukewarm water since Sunday, and there's a small puddle under it. No gas smell. ZIP is 94087.

Thanks, that helps. A 12-year-old gas tank that's both lukewarm and leaking is near the end of a typical tank's life. Here's what a plumber will look at:

- Where the water is coming from. A drip from a fitting, the drain valve or the relief valve can often be fixed. Water from the tank itself usually means it needs to be replaced.
- Why the water is lukewarm. Common causes are heavy sediment buildup, a burner or thermocouple problem, or a broken dip tube.

Until someone comes:
- Put a towel or pan under the puddle and keep an eye on it.
- If the leak gets worse, shut the cold-water valve on the pipe going into the top of the heater. You can also turn the gas control knob to "pilot" or "vacation."
